sections.h2: Where is the Hertford County Register of Deeds and what does it hold?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is on the third floor of the Hertford County Courthouse at 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, in Winton, and the office line is 252-358-7850. Hours are 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday, except county holidays and closings. Winton is the county seat, established in 1766.

The county says its staff record and maintain real estate documents going back as early as 1862. The holdings include deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge records, notary records, and birth, death and marriage records for events that happened in the county. The county's own history page adds that land deeds in the area date to 1710, so a title search on an old family farm can run through several centuries of paper.

Hertford County lies in northeastern North Carolina along the Virginia line. The Census Bureau counts 353.16 square miles of land and 19,015 residents as of July 2025, which works out to roughly 61 people per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: What does the Hertford County fee schedule charge to record?
sections.html:
The county posts its fees with a note that they are subject to change, and the real estate amounts line up with the statewide schedule. Payment can be made by cash, check, money order or credit or debit card, and mailed documents need a self-addressed stamped envelope for return.

Real estate recording charges on the Hertford County Register of Deeds fee schedule
ItemCharge as posted
Deeds and instruments in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000.00, based on purchase price
Satisfactions and cancellationsNo fee
Plat$21.00 per page
Non-standard document$25.00 per document
Multiple instruments in one document$10.00 added
Uncertified copies$.25 per page

Certified copies are $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page. Plat copies are $3.00 per page, and a certified copy of a military discharge is free.

sections.h2: What recording rules should a Hertford County seller know about?
sections.html:
Hertford County enforces the statewide standards in G.S. 161-14 and posts them on its recording rules page. A deed that fails them can still be recorded, but the office adds the $25.00 nonstandard document fee.

  • Paper must be 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches, typed or printed in black on white, text on one side only.
  • The first page needs a blank top margin of at least three inches, and the other margins must be at least half an inch.
  • Type must be at least 10 point, and the type of instrument is stated at the top of the first page.
  • The first page of a deed or deed of trust must bear the name of the person or law firm that drafted it, a rule that comes from Session Law 2011-351.

The county also asks that deeds carry a tax department parcel number. Each deed needs either a signed statement from the tax department that no delinquent taxes are owed, or the sentence that delinquent taxes, if any, are to be paid by the closing attorney to the county tax collector from closing proceeds. Every deed recorded electronically must include that delinquent tax statement.

sections.h2: Can I e-record a Hertford County deed?
sections.html:
Yes. The county's FAQ says it e-records every document except maps, and it works through two submitters, Corporation Service Company (CSC) and Simplifile. Each lists a support line and email on the county's e-recording page.

The county explains that e-recording delivers documents from the submitter to the office without leaving the submitter's desk, and the recorded document comes back electronically right after recording. Ask your closing attorney which submitter they plan to use. Walk-in recording at the Winton courthouse is the other route, and any document you want returned by mail needs a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Staff cannot perform title searches, because North Carolina law prohibits it, and they cannot tell you whether a lien sits on your property. A deed of trust recorded in the office is the sign that the property was used to borrow money. Changes to a recorded deed cannot be made at the counter either; a new deed has to be prepared, and the office recommends seeing an attorney.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax in a Hertford County sale?
sections.html:
The seller. North Carolina G.S. 105-228.30 requires the transferor to pay the tax to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded.

The statute sets the rate at one dollar for each five hundred dollars, or fractional part, of the consideration, and Hertford County prints the same rate on its schedule as $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price. The county keeps half, and the other half goes to the Department of Revenue. A closing attorney deducts it from the seller's proceeds, so look for it on your settlement statement. The statute is at G.S. 105-228.30.

Recording itself matters because G.S. 47-18 makes a conveyance effective against lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies. See G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Hertford County homes?
sections.html:
Hertford County has a low-value housing market and a shrinking population. QuickFacts shows a 2020 Census count of 21,552 and a July 2025 estimate of 19,015, a drop of 11.8 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing units, 2020 to 2024: $119,200
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 67.4 percent
  • Median gross rent: $844
  • Median household income: $45,537
  • Housing units in July 2025: 9,873
  • Building permits in 2025: 3

Only three building permits were issued in 2025. Agriculture remains the foundation of the economy according to the county, with tobacco, cotton, peanuts, corn and soybeans listed as staples, and the Chowan River runs through the county.

sections.h2: What should I check before recording a deed in Hertford County?
sections.html:
Start with the title. Staff cannot search it for you, so use an attorney, then confirm the deed and any release are ready to record. Records are indexed by name, not by street address, so the office cannot tell you who owns a property from an address. Land Records Mapping handles address and parcel questions, and estate, will or divorce records sit with the Clerk of Superior Court.

  • Have any paid-off deed of trust satisfied of record; the satisfaction carries no fee.
  • Collect the parcel number from the tax office so the deed carries it.
  • Ask the tax collector about the current year's bill, since a listing for January 1 stays with the owner of record on that date.
  • Review the county's warnings on deed scams and fraud detection, which are linked from the Register of Deeds page.

The county's tax assessor and tax collector offices are at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. A countywide revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my recorded deed in Hertford County?
faqs.a: Yes. Copies are available in person or through the county sites, and all real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be. A certified copy costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

faqs.q: How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A general deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each added page, per the county's posted schedule. A deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages. The county notes that fees are subject to change, so call before you send payment.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a Hertford County deed?
faqs.a: The county lists it as $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, matching the state rate of one dollar per $500. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What happens if my Hertford County deed is not formatted correctly?
faqs.a: The office records it anyway and adds a $25.00 nonstandard document fee. Check the margin, paper size, type size and drafter name rules first to avoid the extra charge.

faqs.q: Can Hertford County staff search my title?
faqs.a: No. The county's own FAQ says North Carolina General Statutes prohibit Register of Deeds staff from performing title searches, so hire an attorney or title professional for that work.
